en.title: Collision Course: Is Netflix's Spanish Heist Thriller Worth Your Time?
en.summary: A bank robbery in Madrid spirals into a high-concept thriller with a twisty narrative. We break down whether this Spanish Netflix original lives up to its ambitious premise.
en.body:
Netflix is no stranger to a good heist story, and their latest Spanish offering, **Collision Course** (or *Colisión*), attempts to deliver just that with a dash of noir and a high-concept twist. Directed by **Daniel Sánchez Arévalo**, the film plunges viewers into the heart of Madrid during a turbulent economic period more than a decade ago. The backdrop is crucial: a housing market collapse, risky bank loans, and widespread foreclosures set the stage for desperation and resentment. This crisis directly fuels the motive behind the audacious bank robbery at the film's core, even involving a bank director whose institution was at the forefront of the financial meltdown.

The film's clever premise lies in its revelation that several members of the heist crew are also presiding over the investigation. This insider knowledge could allow them to conceal evidence or escape unnoticed. However, as is often the case in these narratives, the plan goes spectacularly wrong. Instead of a clean getaway with the intended diamonds, the robbers find themselves in a chaotic car crash. This pivotal event is where **Collision Course** injects its most intriguing, high-concept element, linking all five main characters in ways that are best experienced firsthand.

## A Heist Gone Wrong

What begins as a seemingly straightforward bank heist quickly devolves into a tense game of deception, fear, and survival. The tight space staging and focus on every decision and gesture add to the gripping nature of the thriller. While some reviews hail it as an enjoyable popcorn thriller, others find its narrative structure somewhat confusing, suggesting that the film prioritizes its ambitious concept over absolute clarity. The critical reception is mixed, highlighting that while the premise is undeniably intriguing, the execution might not land perfectly for every viewer.

## The Verdict for Fans

For fans of twisty thrillers and narrative puzzles, **Collision Course** presents a compelling proposition. The Spanish film industry has consistently delivered high-quality genre content, and **Daniel Sánchez Arévalo**'s involvement adds a layer of directorial pedigree. The film's exploration of the fallout from the 2008 financial crisis offers a grounded, relatable motive for the heist, while the high-concept element promises to keep audiences guessing. However, those who prefer straightforward narratives might find themselves occasionally lost in the film's complexities. It’s a gamble that could pay off handsomely for viewers seeking something beyond the typical heist fare, but it’s wise to go in expecting a film that challenges as much as it entertains.

## What's Next

**Collision Course** was released on Netflix on October 30, 2026. While there’s no immediate word on sequels or further projects directly related to this film, the success of Spanish thrillers on the platform often leads to more opportunities for creators and actors involved.

content_raw: Picture Credit: Netflix If La Casa De Papel and numerous other series are any indication, Netflix programming is really fond of serving a twisty heist for its subscribers. And this fall’s entry comes—once again—from Spain, from acclaimed director Daniel Sánchez Arévalo. But should you chase the thrills from this new thriller with a bit of noir and high-concept ideas thrown in? The action of Collision Course is happening more than a decade ago, in a fraught time for the Spanish economy. Banks started to sell risky housing loans to impoverished populations, who often signed long-term arrangements with no information on the caveats. When the housing market tumbled down and banks had to ask for a bailout, clients could not pay the money back, and massive asset seizures happened, leading to tens of thousands of Spanish residents out of a home. That crisis affected a couple of characters in the movie, but most important is the overarching motive for the heist we see. And it even involves one of the bank directors whose—fictional—bank was front row for the crisis. The perfect heist often involves accomplices on the inside; and one of the great ideas of this movie is that it is soon revealed that most of the five characters in Collision Course are presiding over the investigation, which has the potential for them to conceal evidence or know when to bail out without a trace; only the heist goes very wrong and messy from the get-go. The group does not leave with the contents of a safe which were supposed to have diamonds in them, but also gets into a car crash. This car crash launches the high-concept element of Collision Course : even though it is linked to each of the five main characters, the way it unfolds is best left to discover for yourself, as this review contains no major spoilers . It is safe to say Collision Course is heavy on its plot, and sometimes enamored with its twists, and light on character work. We only learn about the motivations and traumas of the characters through the aftermath of the heist, and the high-concept device means that the audience also has to pay extra attention to what unfolds on screen. That also means we don’t have a lot of involvement for the respective lives of Carla ( Laia Costa ) and Tomás ( Tamar Novas ), a couple on the ropes, or the motives of retired cop Pedro (character actor Karra Elejalde ). But it does not really matter, as the reveals and betrayals are coming fast and furious during the movie. Picture Credit: Netflix The photography lacks something distinctive from other heist movies, and the visual ideas are few and far between. Still, Collision Course strives to make a point with its film noir themes of middle-class citizens with scarce resources trying to make a clean getaway by all means necessary; the diversion that lets the robbers enter the bank sees one old man trying to cash in on his (fake) €5 million lottery ticket.
